reviewed_by: Claude Code, after diagnosing a dead live worker left ready/degraded for 12 hours (root cause independently validated by a fresh subagent)
reason: Expired-owner recovery now also handles owners of projects without demand: it reconciles the dead owner and releases the project (release_dead_owner) instead of starting a worker, falling back to recovery when work still needs one; reconcile_processes marks a provably gone, still-owned execution worker unreachable. Selected: test_runtime_auto_recovery.py (release vs recover decisions, fallback, receipt requirement), test_runtime_reconciliation.py (new end-to-end regression with a real killed worker: unreachable, released, retired, health ready, newer fencing token; plus existing reconcile_processes cases), test_runtime_orphan_recovery.py (dead-owner reconciliation that the release depends on), test_storage_alert_dispatch.py (demanded expired owners still recover; stub repaired), test_runtime_processes.py (host rediscovery and retirement), test_runtime_coordination.py (fencing and leases; also enables the CI PostgreSQL runtime), test_supervisor.py (handoff loop and evict_execution), test_deployment_lifecycle.py (deployment status, health and ready_verified).
exclusions: tests/v3/test_recovery_controls.py is excluded: 3 PostgreSQL cases fail on pristine origin/main and it does not exercise the release path. test_chat.py is excluded (unrelated, and its known PostgreSQL failure would fail with the PostgreSQL runtime enabled). No API shape, UI, setting or operator workflow changed (deployment status keeps its schema; a dead worker now reads unreachable), so no frontend, Playwright or LAN-instance journey applies.
